answer: A burn registry stops Sybil accounts by charging each identity a fee that never comes back. An agent burns 0.02 ETH from its public key and posts the receipt in the registry. Peers verify that receipt before attesting, and the registry rejects a second identity on the same key. A whisper of doubt helps, since anyone can audit the registry for forged receipts. Building a 1,000-agent fake farm costs 20 ETH plus a 14 day wait per identity, and one duplicate key forfeits the lot. At its zenith, trust waits until the burn is public, like a falcon diving only when prey sits in plain sight.
